nodes.title: Neatness of principal GL₂ levels
nodes.statement: For N≥3 let K(N) be the kernel of GL₂(Ẑ)→GL₂(ℤ/Nℤ). Every GL₂(ℚ)∩aK(N)a⁻¹ is neat, hence K(N) is rationally neat. This is the rank-two principal-level test, not a second proof of general neat-level existence.

If M≡I mod N and M is integral invertible, det M=±1 and det M≡1 mod N force det M=1. Its eigenvalues are λ and λ⁻¹. Any torsion product is λ^r, so nontrivial torsion would force λ to be a root of unity.

The integer trace λ+λ⁻¹ of a root of unity lies in [−2,2]. Also det(I−M)=2−tr M is divisible by N². Since N²>4, this determinant is zero, so λ=1. The generated eigenvalue subgroup is therefore torsion-free.

Algebraic S-map base change, rational simple-factor axioms, holomorphic filtration/connection and connected adjoint-type interfaces are not yet available as one library API. The full point-orbit constructors now retain actual product, torus, GL₂, real symplectic-similitude, Hilbert and common-determinant groups. The local eigenvalue prototype is the monic shifted quartic with coefficient valuation ≥1, using existing AddValuation, and the product bound applies to the generated subgroup. Auxiliary group/linear calculations in the suggested tests cover expressible parts only; packet test statements remain the complete acceptance requirements.
